mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is positively associated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as low rates compress equity discount rates and increase present value of future cash flows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns when FEDFUNDS is at 2.4%.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% signals economic weakness and reduced corporate earnings potential, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns when UNRATE is above 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: The joint rise in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%) and CPI (CPIAUCSL > 250) indicates overheating economy and imminent rate hikes, compressing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and CPIAUCSL > 250.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and CPIAUCSL > 250), central bank policy shifts to combat inflation, increasing equity discount rates and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns during monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and CPIAUCSL > 250).
